title: Dungeon Finder
content: The Dungeon Finder (patch 3.3, December 2009) automatically groups players across realms for a chosen dungeon or a random one, through a queue where each player selects the Tank, Healer, and/or Damage role they'll fill. Once a group forms, everyone is teleported directly to the dungeon entrance, and abandoning the run before the group agrees to disband applies the Dungeon Deserter debuff. Queuing for a random Northrend heroic is the most common use: the first one completed each day awards 2 Emblems of Frost, and every additional one that day awards 2 Emblems of Triumph instead, making it the fastest way to gear up at level 80.

title: Heroic Dungeons and Emblems
content: Heroic difficulty unlocks at level 80 for every Northrend five-man dungeon, with no attunement or key required as there was in the Burning Crusade -- just queue for it. Heroics and raids pay Emblems rather than gold-bought tokens; by patch 3.3.5 the two currencies actually being earned are Emblem of Triumph (heroics, Trial of the Crusader, and repeat random-dungeon wins) and Emblem of Frost (Icecrown Citadel and the day's first random heroic). The earlier Emblem of Heroism, Valor, and Conquest from Naxxramas, Ulduar, and Trial of the Crusader's launch are no longer dropped, having been superseded as raid content advanced. Emblems are spent with quartermasters in Dalaran and Icecrown for current-tier epic gear.

title: Dual Talent Specialization
content: Dual talent specialization (patch 3.1) lets a character save two separate talent builds -- each with its own glyphs and action bars -- and swap between them outside combat. It costs 1000 gold, requires level 40, and is bought once from your class trainer; after that, switching between the two saved specs is free and unlimited. Players commonly keep one PvE spec and one PvP spec, or a tank/healer spec alongside a damage spec, and swap depending on what the group needs.

title: Cold Weather Flying
content: Cold Weather Flying is the extra skill needed to use a flying mount in Northrend; Expert or Artisan riding alone isn't enough there. It's trained from a flying trainer in Dalaran or the Storm Peaks for 1,000 gold at level 77. A level 80 can buy the Tome of Cold Weather Flight for 1,000 gold and mail it to an alt, letting that alt fly in Northrend from 68.

title: Death Knight Runes and Runic Power
content: Death Knights don't use mana, rage or energy: they have six runes, two Blood, two Frost and two Unholy, plus a Runic Power bar. Spending a rune casts its ability and puts that rune on a short recharge, and spending runes builds the Runic Power that fuels abilities like Death Coil. As Wrath's hero class, every Death Knight starts at level 55.

title: Vehicle Combat
content: Vehicles are a Wrath of the Lich King addition: mountable siege engines, cannons, and creatures that swap a player's normal action bars for the vehicle's own abilities for as long as they're in the seat. They show up throughout the expansion -- Ulduar's Flame Leviathan fight, the cannons defending Wintergrasp and Isle of Conquest, the siege engines and demolishers of Strand of the Ancients, and mine-cart or turret sections tucked into several dungeons. Leaving a vehicle returns a player to their normal spellbook immediately, and most vehicles can be destroyed out from under their rider by enemy fire.
